title: Real-Time Streaming and WebSocket Subscriptions Layer
summary: Deliver authorised project-scoped state-change notifications with bounded replay and recovery while keeping API resources and ledger events authoritative.

intent.statement: Keep authorised clients current through durable, safe notifications without making WebSocket delivery a source of engineering truth.
desired_outcomes: Each stream session is identity and project/channel scoped.
Clients recover safely through cursor replay or authoritative API resynchronisation.
Slow or disconnected clients cannot impair other project/session delivery.

success_measures.name: Authorised delivery
success_measures.target: 0 cross-project or unauthorised channel deliveries in security suite
success_measures.measurement_method: Run subscription and mid-session revocation negative tests.

success_measures.name: Safe recovery
success_measures.target: 100% reconnect fixtures result in replay or explicit resync-required response

provenance.rationale: Real-time delivery must preserve platform evidence and project isolation.

problem.statement: Clients need timely project updates, but naive WebSocket delivery can leak cross-project data, lose/reorder events, exhaust runtime memory or be confused with authoritative state.
problem.current_state: AGASTYA defines API and evidence contracts but has no session, channel, cursor, replay or backpressure protocol for real-time clients.
impact: Users may see stale operation/approval/validation state.
Reconnects can cause unsafe duplicate/out-of-order UI changes.
WebSocket runtime may become a tenant-isolation or resource-exhaustion risk.

evidence.label: Approved Unified API Gateway and Client SDK Layer

business_context.business_value: Safe streaming reduces stale interface state and improves operator response without weakening AGASTYA's specification/evidence control plane.

stakeholders.name: Security Engineering
stakeholders.role: Owns session/channel authorisation and data classification

actors.name: Authorised Client
goals: Subscribe to permitted project state changes.

actors.name: Streaming Gateway
goals: Validate tickets, subscriptions and delivery policies.

actors.name: Event Fan-out Service
goals: Transform authoritative event sources into safe channel events.

functional_requirements.title: Issue scoped connection tickets
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall issue short-lived Gateway-authorised connection tickets and establish sessions only after identity, tenant/project scope, channel policy and expiration validation.

functional_requirements.title: Allow only registered project channels
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall maintain a registered channel catalogue and permit only exact authorised project-scoped subscriptions.

functional_requirements.title: Fan out authoritative source events
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall produce stream events from authoritative outbox or ledger-derived sources with stream ID, source reference, cursor, correlation ID, channel and safe payload.

provenance.rationale: Delivery plane derives from evidence-backed event source.

functional_requirements.title: Support cursor replay and resynchronisation
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall provide bounded replay/resume by project/channel cursor and emit RESYNC_REQUIRED when safe replay cannot be provided.

functional_requirements.title: Apply bounded backpressure
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall enforce bounded buffers, acknowledgement and heartbeat policy, rate limits and slow-consumer handling for each session.

provenance.rationale: Avoid one slow connection exhausting streaming runtime.

functional_requirements.title: Protect payload and session access
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall validate/redact/classify stream payloads, terminate subscriptions on expiry or policy revocation, and record safe session/delivery evidence.

provenance.rationale: Prevent data leakage and stale permissions.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Delivery shall be at-least-once within retained replay window, with ordering only per project/channel partition and explicit resync outside retention.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Reconnect and duplicate/out-of-order channel tests validate cursor and resync semantics.
non_functional_requirements.target: Every reconnect fixture produces replay or explicit resync state.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Stream messages, telemetry and control frames shall not reveal secret material, private reasoning, internal stack traces or cross-project/classification-disallowed data.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Payload transformation and session security suite inspects allowed/denied delivery fixtures.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero prohibited fields delivered in security fixtures.

business_rules.statement: A subscription names exactly one registered channel and one authorised project; wildcard, arbitrary event-filter and cross-project subscriptions are denied.
A cursor is monotonic only within its project/channel partition; if unavailable or unauthorised, runtime sends RESYNC_REQUIRED and client must re-read authoritative API.
Clients may not publish authoritative platform events through streaming channel and stream delivery cannot bypass Gateway, Ledger, classification or policy controls.

provenance.rationale: Delivery is not a command/source-of-truth path.

constraints.statement: Initial streaming supports registered status/summary channels with API fallback; client publishing, arbitrary topics, raw audit replay, presence and collaboration are excluded.
constraints.rationale: Bound initial real-time surface until session, recovery and data-classification controls are proven.

dependencies.name: Persistent streaming runtime and replay store
dependencies.risk: Runtime topology must support persistent connections, bounded session state and authorised fan-out.

bounded_contexts.name: Real-Time Delivery
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own connection tickets, sessions, channel registry, cursor replay, backpressure and delivery evidence.

ubiquitous_language.definition: Safe channel-specific delivery message derived from authoritative source event.
Monotonic delivery position within one project/channel partition.
Control outcome requiring an authoritative API re-read before streaming resumes.

workflows.name: Authorised reconnecting subscription
workflows.trigger: Client requests a registered project channel with optional last cursor.

steps.action: Validates short-lived ticket, session identity and channel/project capability.
steps.result: Session/subscription is allowed or denied without disclosure.

steps.action: Checks cursor retention and delivery partition.
steps.result: Retained events replay or RESYNC_REQUIRED emits.

steps.action: Delivers filtered events under bounded buffer/ack policy.
steps.result: Client applies idempotent notification or resyncs through API.

outcomes: Client is current without treating WebSocket payload as authoritative state.
workflows.error_handling: Expired/revoked/slow session is terminated or requires resync with metadata-only evidence.

states.name: RESYNC_REQUIRED
states.description: Client must re-read API before resuming relevant channel.

states.name: CLOSING
states.description: Expiry, revocation or backpressure close in progress.

security_requirements.statement: Streaming session and subscription authorisation shall enforce exact identity, project/channel scope, expiry, classification and immediate policy revocation without exposing cross-project data.
security_requirements.verification_method: Security tests cover wrong-project channel, ticket replay, expiry, mid-session membership removal and unsafe source payload.

observability_requirements.statement: Session, subscription, delivery, cursor, replay, resync, backpressure, revocation and disconnect outcomes shall emit correlated safe evidence events.
observability_requirements.verification_method: End-to-end trace reconstructs client session from ticket to disconnect without unsafe payload.

acceptance_criteria.title: Scoped session is created
acceptance_criteria.given: Authenticated project member requests allowed ticket/channel.
acceptance_criteria.then: Session binds exact project/channel, expiry and correlation evidence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Invalid project/channel is denied
acceptance_criteria.given: User requests unregistered or other-project channel.

acceptance_criteria.title: Fan-out carries safe provenance
acceptance_criteria.then: Stream event contains source reference, ID, cursor, channel and safe classified payload.

acceptance_criteria.title: Reconnect replays or requires resync
acceptance_criteria.given: Client reconnects inside or outside retained window.
acceptance_criteria.then: It receives at-least-once replay or RESYNC_REQUIRED.

acceptance_criteria.title: Slow client is bounded
acceptance_criteria.given: Client stops acknowledging and buffer reaches limit.
acceptance_criteria.then: Runtime bounds backpressure and closes/resyncs without impact to other sessions.

acceptance_criteria.title: Revoked membership terminates channel
acceptance_criteria.then: Affected channel terminates and future messages are withheld.

acceptance_criteria.title: Unsafe source payload is withheld
acceptance_criteria.then: Delivery is denied/quarantined and prohibited material is not emitted.

test_requirements.expected_evidence: Bound session record and safe lifecycle events.

test_requirements.scope: Wrong project/channel, ticket replay, expiry and mid-session revocation.

test_requirements.expected_evidence: Safe event fixtures linked to authoritative source references.

test_requirements.scope: Cursor replay, duplicate-event deduplication and resync fallback.

test_requirements.expected_evidence: Slow-consumer test demonstrates bounded resource use and unaffected peer session.
Withheld event and safe evidence record.

risks.title: Persistent runtime or buffer design creates availability/isolation failure
risks.description: Unbounded sessions or incorrect routing could degrade delivery and leak data.
risks.mitigation: Default-deny channel scope, bounded buffers, explicit cursor semantics, persistent runtime ADR and security/load testing.

open_questions.question: Which managed runtime/topology supports persistent sessions, authorised fan-out and replay storage?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Streaming service deployment cannot be selected.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Persistent runtime, routing and replay topology ADR is mandatory before deployment.

open_questions.question: What retention, buffer, event-size and connection/subscription quota policy applies?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Replay and operational bounds cannot be finalised.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Retention, buffer, event-size and quota policy is mandatory before channel enablement.

architecture_decisions.title: Use Gateway-authorised WebSockets with bounded at-least-once channel delivery
architecture_decisions.context: Clients need timely updates but persistent delivery must not become a source of truth or bypass project/policy/evidence controls.
architecture_decisions.decision: Issue short-lived connection tickets through Gateway, subscribe to registered project channels, fan out ledger-derived events with cursors and require API re-read when replay is unavailable.

alternatives.name: Unscoped generic pub-sub
alternatives.summary: Let clients choose arbitrary topics and broker events directly.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Cannot enforce stable project/classification policy or safe source provenance.

alternatives.name: Exactly-once global ordered stream
alternatives.summary: Promise total order and one delivery globally.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Disproportionate complexity and unnecessary for resource-notification use cases.

architecture_decisions.rationale: Bounded at-least-once per-channel delivery plus API fallback provides resilient UX while retaining platform truth model.
consequences: Client SDK must expose dedup/resync model.
Persistent runtime and quota policies require ADR decisions.

provenance.rationale: Streaming event must derive from durable ledger/outbox evidence.

coverage_summary.method: Initial streaming draft mapping; implementation coverage is not yet applicable.
